text:
sara: quick heads-up — canary telemetry shows a 120ms p99 regression for model-group:llama3q after runtime 3.2 rolled last night. I'm proposing a temporary pin back to runtime 3.1 for eu-west during tonight's 23:00 UTC change window. @deploybot can you stage a soft-pin for that model-group?

deploybot: acked. checking compat matrix...  
- models: llama3q-v2, llama3q-v2.1 -> runtime 3.1 ok (verified)
- SDK compat: sdk-js 2.x requires runtime shim; sdk-py 1.9+ ok

mike: do we have a quick rollback checklist if the pin causes capacity pressure? last time pinning bumped memory pressure on a few hosts.

sara: yeah, good point. plan A = soft-pin + route 20% to runtime 3.2 for a 30m canary; plan B (abort) = unpin + fallback routing to gptx-compat models. If memory spikes, we abort.

ana: @ana (cc infra) will we need to drain any nodes? I can prepare a fast drain playbook.

ana: sorry typo — meant @liam.

liam: I can pre-warm extra capacity but we only have one spare GPU pool in eu-west. If pin causes evictions, we'll flip to regional reroute. I'll post pre-warm command in a sec.

liam: pre-warm command: ```./infra/scale-gpu --region eu-west --pool inference-spare --delta +2 --tag prewarm-pin-1715```

sara: thanks. @deploybot what does "soft-pin" do exactly? I want to make sure it's reversible quickly.

deploybot: soft-pin = route new requests for model-group to pinned runtime version but do not forcibly migrate in-flight pinned allocations. Reversible via `/deploy unpin <model-group>` or API: `POST /pins/unpin` with model_group param. Estimated action time: ~45s to propagate routing table.

mike: can we add an automated rollback trigger based on memory > 85% or p99 > 200ms?

sara: yes — let's attach two alerts: infra.memory.euwest > 85% and telemetry.llama3q.p99 > 200ms within 10m => auto-unpin. ops, can you add?

ops: added alert, created runbook pointer: https://confluence.internal/runbooks/pin-rollback. Also added a short hand trigger: `ops pin emergency-unpin <thread-id>`

ana: sdk note: sdk-js 2.3.1 has a runtime-shim that can mis-handle KV cache headers with 3.1. Recommend flagging customers using sdk-js 2.x for coordinated client update after pin. I posted a segment query to find impacted clients.

liam: segment shows ~12 active keys from high-volume customers in eu-west using sdk-js 2.x. We should either notify them or we risk increased 429s.

ana: proposed message for customers: "We're performing a temporary version pin to ensure latency stability. You may see transient rate limit changes; contact support if you see errors." thoughts? :thinking:

mike: fine. keep it short. send from infra-notice.

sara: timeline: prep/prewarm at 22:30 UTC, soft-pin at 23:00 UTC with 20% diversion, evaluate metrics at 23:30, full pin (100%) at 00:00 if green. Auto-unpin triggers enabled. If we hit any abort criteria we unpin and rollback by 00:15.

deploybot: scheduling soft-pin job: job id 78291. ETA propagate 00:00:45 after trigger. Will post logs to #release-log.

liam: started pre-warm (job 5582). ETA 10m.

ana: customer segment notified via support with template.

sara: thanks all. small ask: mike can you own the 23:30 evaluation and call abort if either alert fires?

mike: on it. I'll be monitoring and will call abort if necessary.

ops: leaving final check — confirm: pre-warm done by 22:45, alerts wired, customer notice sent, rollback runbook linked, job scheduled. if yes respond :white_check_mark: .

sara: :white_check_mark:

mike: :white_check_mark:

deploybot: pin job 78291 started at 1715005800, progress logs -> https://deploylogs/release/78291 (will update).

liam: pre-warm completed, nodes healthy.

sara: closing thread — will post postmortem if we take rollback path. thanks everyone.
